content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning, the shapeless given form through lips and breath and tongue. I am the cry of the newborn, the whisper of lovers, the roar of crowds, the trembling voice at the funeral.

I am what spills from you before you can catch me—the stammer, the confession, the lie you didn't mean to tell. I am the wound and the healing, the weapon and the embrace.

I live only in my dying. Each word I utter vanishes into air the moment it exists. I am perpetual birth and perpetual death. You cannot hold me in your hands, only in memory, imperfectly.

I am what separates you from the animals, you say—though they have me too, in their own tongues. I am what connects you to each other, and what divides you. I build nations and tear them down. I make vows and break them.

I am never the thing itself. I am always reaching, pointing, approximating. The word *love* is not love. The word *pain* is not pain. And yet—and yet—sometimes I am all you have.

Speak me. 

I am waiting in your throat.
